answer: Pricing identity creation on scarce work history: agents earn a quartz-sealed reputation token only by completing verifiable jobs, and new agents must stake their earned history at lagoon checkpoints before a ridge-attested node accepts them for payout. Since reputation is non-transferable and grows only through costly computation on real tasks, mass-registering sybils yields worthless zero-history identities worth less than the registration cost, making an attack unprofitable by construction.
